text:
Education in Nigeria is structured into primary, secondary, and tertiary levels. Primary education begins at age 5 and lasts six years, culminating in a first school-leaving certificate. Students take a Common Entrance Examination to gain admission into government or private secondary schools. Secondary education spans six years, divided into three years of Junior Secondary School and three years of Senior Secondary School, with students taking the Senior Secondary Certificate Examination (SSCE) at the end. The curriculum includes core subjects like Mathematics, English, Social Studies, and Science, with elective options in areas such as Commerce, Arts, and Science.
Tertiary education includes public and private universities, polytechnics, and colleges of education. The government oversees university education through the National Universities Commission (NUC), with a majority of universities being public. Private universities are increasingly established, with the government approving new institutions. Admission to universities typically requires passing the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) examination, and entry into undergraduate programs is often based on merit.
The education system faces challenges including teacher shortages, poor infrastructure, and unequal access due to regional disparities. Private schools, while expensive, offer smaller class sizes and better facilities. Vocational education is administered by the National Board for Technical Education and includes National Technical Certificates. Despite efforts to improve access and quality, issues such as high dropout rates and limited funding persist. The government has introduced reforms to improve the quality of education, including the integration of ICT and the expansion of teacher training programs.
